newsitem.title: USA: CellPro facing $16.9 mln suit over patent.
newsitem.headline: CellPro facing $16.9 mln suit over patent.

text.p: Johns Hopkins University, Becton Dickinson and Co, and Baxter International Inc said Tuesday that they have filed motions in federal district court in Delaware seeking additional damages, attorneys' fees and a permanent injunction to enforce two stem cell selection technology patents infringed by CellPro Inc

In addition to injunctive relief, Johns Hopkins, Becton Dickinson and Baxter said they are are seeking treble damages, in the total amount of $6.9 million, and reimbursement of approximately $7 million of litigation expenses that were incurred as a result of CellPro's willful infringement of the patents.

In March, the two companies and the university said, a federal jury found that CellPro had willfully infringed two patents covering CD34 monoclonal antibodies and purified stem cells, and awarded them $2.3 million in damages.
CellPro respresentatives were not immediately available for comment.
